concepts.preferred_label: Pulmonary Atresia with Ventricular Septal Defect
concepts.why: The patient has pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect and a patent ductus arteriosus, as shown by echocardiography.
The patient has a provisional diagnosis of immune thrombocytopenia and has a low platelet count with a prolonged platelet aggregation time.
The patient has cyanosis with low oxygen saturation, which is a sign of a respiratory or cardiac issue.
The patient has a patent ductus arteriosus, as shown by echocardiography.
The patient has a ventricular septal defect, as shown by echocardiography.
The patient has respiratory distress with low oxygen saturation, which is a sign of a respiratory issue.
The patient has a low platelet count, which is a sign of thrombocytopenia.
The patient has a congenital heart defect, as shown by echocardiography.

rationales.F01: Low oxygen saturation is a key feature of cyanosis.
rationales.F03: Thrombocytopenia is characterized by a low platelet count.
rationales.F05: Pulmonary atresia with ventricular septal defect is a congenital heart defect.
rationales.F08: A high platelet count is not typical of immune thrombocytopenia.
rationales.F11: Prolonged platelet aggregation time can be seen in immune thrombocytopenia.
rationales.F12: A provisional diagnosis of immune thrombocytopenia was made based on clinical findings.
